frequency_question: How often do central banks with such statutory powers decide to implement an incremental reserve ratio instrument within a given multi-month horizon when faced with excess liquidity?
membership_rule: Members are central banks in major emerging economies (e.g., India, Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa) possessing direct statutory authority over reserve ratios, explicitly choosing to activate an incremental/special CRR tool. Excluded are standard routine adjustments to baseline reserve requirements or open market operations.
window: Any designated 4-month operational window within a monetary tightening or liquidity-management cycle.

cases.name: PBoC Reserve Requirement Ratio targeted cuts/hikes cycles (liquidity management tools)
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement adjustments
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement adjustments

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 4 named cases representing distinct emerging market central bank discretionary liquidity absorption episodes.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier economies where statutory frameworks differ significantly.
skeleton: 4 major emerging-market central bank liquidity-management episodes involving targeted reserve ratio interventions over the past 5 years, scaled across comparable liquidity surplus cycles.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 observed comparable policy cycles where the central bank had clear intent and capability.
validity_reason: Central bank statutory powers and operational toolkits for liquidity management remain stable over multi-year horizons barring major legislative overhauls.
